A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Evaluation Agent and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and Appendices A–E. Added sections and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark-agreement, timing, sample-size, and backbone experiments, plus a user study and open-ended evaluation cases in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 2–10, the sample-size analysis, and qualitative evaluation and failure cases.

M1.justification: The agents, proposal/execution loop, evaluation toolkit, and VQA procedure remain unchanged. New Appendix E.2 elaborates safeguards: v1 already required stopping justifications in A.1 and depicted framework-enforced stopping in Figure 8.

E1.justification: Both retain 15 VBench dimensions, four T2I-CompBench dimensions, the 100-query dataset, and the same image/video evaluation scenarios. Newly cited benchmarks such as VBench-2.0 and T2V-CompBench are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The comparisons against VBench and T2I-CompBench and the GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini backbone evaluations are retained. The agent evaluators newly discussed in Appendix D.3 do not enter experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The evaluated models, benchmark-tool and prompt restrictions, five performance tiers, and sample-size settings remain unchanged. Appendix B clarifies the existing scoring procedure without reporting a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The 30-prompt sensitivity test, alternative-backbone experiments, Gemini failure cases, and open-ended case studies are retained. Appendix E.2 adds discussion of safeguards, without a new ablation, robustness test, or failure example.

E5.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 6 retain prediction percentages over ten trials with exact-range and one-range-tolerance reporting. No additional run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 2–10 retain their numerical results, and the plotted findings and qualitative cases are unchanged. For example, Table 5 still reports 8 minutes and 26 samples per dimension for Evaluation Agent on SDXL.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(2). The expanded scoring explanation introduces no new formal definition, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of efficient, promptable, explainable, and scalable evaluation, comparable benchmark results, and evaluation time reduced to approximately 10% of traditional methods.

C2.justification: New Appendix E.2 explains how reasoning and stopping constraints mitigate agent failures and identifies fallback design and reliability as remaining work. This adds a specific reliability interpretation; the Gemini failure observations and context-window explanation already existed.

D1.justification: Appendix B more explicitly documents metric-score conversion into tiers and aggregation across rounds. E.2 discloses a maximum-round constraint without specifying its value. These extend implementation documentation; model versions, temperature, and code-access links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds five cited works. Section 2.1 broadens benchmark references, while new Appendix D.3 discusses Qin et al.'s scene-graph question-answering evaluator and VideoGen-Eval. This is a limited expansion of research context rather than a wholesale repositioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites part of Appendix B, adds D.3 and E.2, renumbers the former E.2 as E.3, and adds acknowledgments. Author/contact information and a heading typo are also updated. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The figures and tables retain their content and designs, but appendix figures, notably Figures 6–8, are repositioned. The author block, footnotes, page numbering, and surrounding text layout also change.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through clearer scoring documentation in Appendix B and explicit discussion of stopping safeguards and remaining reliability limitations in E.2. D.3 also acknowledges relevant agent-based evaluators. These are useful, limited gains: empirical support is unchanged, and exact tier thresholds and the round-limit value remain unspecified.
